dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise.

Hi, Denise, hi. Um, my name is Teresa Teixeira, and I'm calling from my cell, so if I cut out, I'm sorry. I'm standing out in my driveway right now, actually, because I just got home from my lunch break, I work over at a dental office, and I only get a half hour, so I came home to let the dog out and that's when I saw it.
Okay, no problem, Teresa. What are you seeing?

So, okay, I rent here. I've been in this place going on three years, and the landlord is great, but he's down in Florida for the winter, so I figured I'd call you folks instead of him. And we had that soaker Wednesday and Thursday, the rain just wouldn't quit, yesterday it was still coming down at, like, supper time. And there's a catch basin at the corner, right near us, and it is just packed with leaves. Like, plastered over the top. And the water can't go down it, so it's backing up and coming right into my driveway.
Gotcha. So the drain at the corner is covered in leaves and the water's pooling instead of draining. Can I get the address?
Yes, sorry, I should have said. It's 322 Bliss Road. We're on the Easton's Beach side, so you come down toward the water and it's the corner right before where the road bends.
322 Bliss Road, okay. And is the water in the driveway just sitting, or is it moving?

That's the thing, it's moving. The driveway slopes a little to the left, and my neighbor, Mr. next door, has a detached garage, and the water's creeping along the edge of my driveway right toward his garage door. I can see it. It's maybe, I don't know, ten, twelve feet from the door? And I'm worried, because if it gets in there, he keeps stuff on the floor, boxes and things. I knocked but nobody's home.
Okay. Is it still raining right now?

No, no, it stopped. It's cloudy, but it stopped last night. That's why it's strange, you know? It should be going down by now, but it's just stuck there because the basin is clogged. I'd go out and pull the leaves off myself, but there's so much water, and I'm in work shoes, and honestly I don't know if I'm even allowed to touch it.
I'd stay out of the street and not wade in, especially with traffic. Leave the clearing to the crew. I'll put in a work order for that basin right now.

Oh, thank you. Okay. And can I ask, do you know when they last came by? To clean it out, I mean. Because I swear I've never seen anybody out here cleaning those, and the leaves have been piling up since November.
Let me pull up the location and see what's on record for that corner. Can you hold on a minute?
Sure, sure, take your time.

Thanks for holding, Teresa. I'm looking at it. I don't see a recent cleaning logged for that basin, nothing I can point to from this fall. That doesn't mean nobody was there, but I can't tell you a date. I'll note on the order that it's backing up toward a neighbor's garage so it gets looked at sooner.

Okay. Okay, that's what I figured. I mean, I'm not trying to blame anybody. I just, I'd hate for him to come home and find water in there. Is there any chance somebody could come today? Because the forecast, I looked this morning, and I think there might be more rain over the weekend.

I can't promise today. Crews are stretched after a storm like that, with a lot of drains calling in. But a basin that's blocked with water heading toward a structure goes near the top of the list. I'll mark it that way.

Okay. That's fair. Thank you. Sorry, I'm just, I get nervous about water. Where I used to live, before here, it was a different town, we had issues, so now whenever I see it moving toward something, I just.
That's understandable. Let me get a couple more details so the crew finds it fast. Which corner is the basin on, relative to your house?

So it's on the corner, on my side of the street. If you're looking at my house from the road, it's to the right, maybe thirty feet down. It's the grate in the curb, the one with the telephone pole right next to it.
Good, that helps. Right side, about thirty feet, grate by the pole. Is there any other drain nearby that's also blocked, or just that one?
Just that one that I can see. The next one down the road looked okay when I drove by, I think. I didn't stop to look closely.
Okay. And what's the best number to reach you if the crew has questions?
It's 401-555-0182. That's my cell. I'll have it on me at work, but I might not pick up if I'm with a patient, so they can leave a message.
Got it, 401-555-0182. I'll put that on the order. Anything else going on at the property? Any water in the house or the garage?

No, thank goodness. Nothing in the house. The water's just in the driveway and the edge of the yard. I have a little shed out back but that's up on blocks. It's just the driveway, and, like I said, it heading over to the neighbor.
Okay. If it does get into his garage or you see it getting close to a door or the house, call back right away and tell whoever answers that it's an update on the open order. They can escalate it.
Okay, I will. Should I, um, put anything down? Like sandbags? I don't have any, but I could get some.
If you've got something on hand, like a towel or a board to nudge water away, sure, but I wouldn't spend money or lift anything heavy over this. The real fix is getting those leaves off the grate.

Right. Okay. That makes sense. Oh, and this is silly, but, while I'm standing here, somebody left a bag of oranges on my porch this morning. Just a bag, no note. I think it's from one of the neighbors, because they do that, but I don't know who. Anyway, I don't know why I'm telling you that.
Well, that's a nice surprise at least. Hopefully they're good ones.
I'll find out tonight. Sorry, I ramble when I'm nervous.

You're fine. You gave me everything I needed. So that's 322 Bliss Road, catch basin at the corner by the pole, clogged with leaves, water backing into your driveway and heading toward the neighbor's garage. Phone is on the order.
Yes, that's exactly it. And you said you couldn't see when they last cleaned it.
Right, nothing recent on my screen. I'll flag that in the notes too, so the crew lead sees there's no record.
Okay, good. Thank you so much, Denise. I have to run back to work, I've got a one o'clock.
Go ahead, you've got time. Take care, Teresa.
You too. Bye.
